prize_parts.citation: For the development of chemically induced protein degradation by induced proximity, from bifunctional PROTACs to the cereblon mechanism of molecular glue degraders

statement.case_for: I keep B057 as my preferred single-part prize. A small molecule that works as a catalytic bridge, recruiting an E3 ligase so that the cell's ubiquitin-proteasome system removes the target, is a new chemical mode of action and not a refinement of occupancy-based inhibition. The ternary-complex mechanism and E3 substrate selectivity are molecularly defined and reproduced across many laboratories and targets, and cereblon as the thalidomide target resolved a decades-old pharmacological puzzle that also underlies glue degraders. Crews and Deshaies supplied the bifunctional PROTAC concept and first demonstrations, and Handa supplied the mechanistic link to the glue class, so the three names span design and mechanism. Round 1 showed that all eight members regard B057 as either the preferred prize or the first alternative, and support came from members with very different backgrounds. That breadth is not a substitute for scientific judgment, but it matches my own reading of the evidence. I treat the absence of an approved degrader as a timing risk, not as a defect in the science: the mechanism is confirmed and generality is shown, and a prize does not need to wait for a drug approval when those conditions hold.
statement.case_against: No degrader is approved, so a prize now rests on confirmed mechanism and late-stage trials and not on delivered therapy. Credit is spread across at least eight people, and a three-name cap leaves out Ciulli, whose structure-guided VHL ligands and ternary-complex work made PROTAC design systematic, as well as Gray, Sakamoto, Ito and Kim. The PROTAC and glue strands have partly separate histories, and one citation risks blurring them. Against that, B054 is mature, has a workable Schultz, Chin and Wang split and no clinical question, and B068 has the cleanest attribution on the list. If the committee judges the timing risk or the attribution blur decisive, I would accept B054 as the fallback.

responses.point: The choice of Handa over Ciulli is a decision about the scope of the discovery, and with no approved degrader he would rather wait than settle credit between two lineages still developing.
responses.response: I agree it is a scope decision and not bookkeeping. After weighing it again I keep Handa. The cereblon finding is the one result that connects the bifunctional and glue strands under one mechanism and the thalidomide history, whereas Ciulli's VHL ligands are an enabling advance within the PROTAC strand. I would take Ciulli over Deshaies only if the committee deliberately narrows the citation to bifunctional degraders, and then the glue strand would go unattributed, which I consider the worse loss. On waiting, I do not think the committee has required approval when mechanism and generality are shown, and the risk of waiting is that the credit question becomes harder as the field grows. I still regard B054 as the most credible fallback you propose.

responses.point: B068 has the cleanest two-person attribution and three decades of verified delivery, while B057 forces a split between the PROTAC design strategy and the cereblon mechanism that a three-name cap makes awkward.
responses.response: The attribution and maturity points are correct, and the split you describe is real. I think the three names cover it, because Crews and Deshaies carry the design strategy and Handa the mechanism, with the cost being that Ciulli, Gray and Sakamoto are left out. On B068, Zou's reply on Kosugi is persuasive, since stoichiometric organotin chemistry of narrow scope is not the general catalytic method. The 2010 point remains my reservation: a C-N coupling prize would honour an additional bond type within a recognised family. I would be comfortable with B068 as a fallback and have moved it into my alternatives for that reason, but not above B057 this year.

responses.point: B068 asks the committee to settle none of the attribution or timing questions that B057 raises, so she prefers it first and would support B057 if the clinical evidence is judged sufficient.
responses.response: That is a fair way to put the trade-off, and your conditional support is useful. My view is that the clinical evidence needed here is that the mechanism holds up and that degraders are in late-stage trials, which I think is met. I accept that B057 leaves some credit disagreement open, which B068 does not. My answer to the chair's fallback question is that if B057 does not reach five votes I would support B054 first, because it has no unresolved clinical or priority question, and B068 second, given the 2010 precedent.

responses.point: The PROTAC and molecular-glue strands have different histories, but he opposes splitting the field into two prizes, and he would keep B016 as an alternative framed with prime editing.
responses.response: I agree with opposing a two-part split. It would need more than three names, and it would spend the whole prize on one area. On B016, I concede the point about prime editing: a base-editing prize now sits close to the 2020 prize and is better framed together with Liu's later work, so I have dropped it from my alternatives in favour of B068, which is the cleaner and more mature reserve.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will accept the lack of an approved degrader as sufficient clinical vindication.
Whether Handa or Ciulli is the better third name, and whether the citation can honour both PROTAC and glue strands without blurring them.
Whether the exclusion of Ciulli, Gray, Sakamoto, Ito and Kim is defensible under the three-name cap.
My recollection of priority and clinical status is not independently verified from the supplied materials.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict has arisen since round 1. My research on dNTP pools and ribonucleotide reductase is not connected to any shortlisted discovery, my profile lists no collaboration or institutional tie with any credited name, and no member has requested recusal.
